q1: WITH S AS (SELECT ID, TIME_SLOT_ID, YEAR FROM TAKES NATURAL JOIN SECTION GROUP BY ID, TIME_SLOT_ID, YEAR HAVING COUNT(TIME_SLOT_ID) > 4) SELECT DISTINCT ID, NAME FROM S NATURAL JOIN STUDENT
q2: WITH S AS (SELECT ID, TIME_SLOT_ID, YEAR FROM TAKES NATURAL JOIN SECTION GROUP BY ID, TIME_SLOT_ID, YEAR HAVING COUNT(TIME_SLOT_ID) > 5) SELECT DISTINCT ID, NAME FROM S NATURAL JOIN STUDENT

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because the HAVING clause in the common table expression (CTE) S has different conditions. Q1 checks for students who have taken more than 4 time slots in a year, while Q2 checks for students who have taken more than 5 time slots in a year. This difference in the number of time slots triggers the difference in the results.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should include students who have taken exactly 4, 5, and 6 time slots in a year. The student who has taken 5 time slots should be in the result of Q1 but not in the result of Q2, and the student who has taken 6 time slots should be in the result of both Q1 and Q2.
